choices: Eckels는 공룡을 보러 6천만 년 전의 정글로 가고 싶어 한다.
items.exp: Eckels는 I've always wanted to see a dinosaur.라고 했고, 6천만 년 전의 정글로 갈 수 있다는 답을 들었어요. 여행 안내원은 Travis이고, Mr. Keith는 새 대통령이에요.
items.passage:
Eckels walked into the office of Time Travel. The big sign on the wall said, "NAME ANY YEAR IN THE PAST. WE TAKE YOU THERE." There was a TV on the wall, and Mr. Keith, the new president, was on the news.
"How can we help you?" said Mr. Parker, the founder of Time Travel.
"I've always wanted to see a dinosaur. Is it possible?" asked Eckels.
"Sure," said Mr. Parker. "We can take you back to the jungle of 60 million years ago."
"Great," said Eckels. "Can you take me there now?"
"You're lucky. There's a time machine that leaves in 10 minutes," said Mr. Parker.
"This is Travis, your travel guide," he continued. "To stay safe, you must follow his instructions."

items.exp: '설립하다'는 found(설립하다) – founded – founded로 변해요. found는 find의 과거형이라 '설립했다'는 뜻으로 쓰지 않아요.
items.passage: Mr. Parker is the person who ( ) Time Travel twenty years ago.

items.q: 밑줄 친 in과 의미가 같은 것은?
choices: She put the book in the box.
The train will arrive in an hour.
I keep a diary in English.
The girl in the red dress is my sister.
The keys are in my bag.
items.exp: 본문의 in 10 minutes는 '10분 후에'라는 뜻이에요. 첫 번째 문장의 in an hour도 '한 시간 후에'예요. 나머지는 장소, 언어, 옷을 입은 상태를 나타내요.
items.passage: There's a time machine that leaves [in] 10 minutes.

items.q: 밑줄 친 that과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: I think that he is kind.
I have a friend that lives in Busan.
He said that she was sick.
items.exp: 본문의 that은 앞의 a time machine을 꾸미는 주격 관계대명사(= which)예요. 첫 번째 문장의 that도 a friend를 꾸미는 관계대명사예요. 나머지는 접속사나 지시대명사·지시형용사예요.
items.passage: There's a time machine [that] leaves in 10 minutes.

items.exp: stay + 형용사는 '~한 상태로 있다'라는 뜻이에요. 부사 calmly가 아니라 형용사 calm을 써요.
items.passage: Just stay ( ).

items.q:
다음 문장의 의미로 알맞은 것은?

You must not run in the hallway.
items.exp: must는 '~해야 한다'이고, must not은 '~하면 안 된다'라는 금지의 뜻이에요. 본문의 You must not leave it at any time.도 같은 뜻이에요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 must와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
items.exp: 의무를 나타내는 must는 have to와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
items.passage: To stay safe, you [must] follow his instructions.

choices: Eckels는 눈을 뜬 채 기계 안을 살폈다.
Eckels는 눈을 감고 앉아 있었고, 몇 분 뒤 기계가 멈췄다.
items.exp: Eckels sat down and closed his eyes. After only a few minutes, the machine stopped.에서 확인할 수 있어요. 다른 여행자는 두 명이었어요.
items.passage:
Inside the time machine, there were two other travelers. Eckels sat down and closed his eyes. He felt the machine moving under his feet. After only a few minutes, the machine stopped.
"We've just arrived in the jungle of 60 million years ago," Travis explained.

items.exp: There were + 복수 명사: ~들이 있었다. two other travelers가 복수이고 이야기가 과거이므로 were를 써요.
items.passage: Inside the time machine, there ( ) two other travelers. Eckels sat down and closed his eyes.

choices: A few people knows the answer.
A little people know the answer.
items.exp: few와 a few는 셀 수 있는 복수 명사와 함께 쓰고 동사도 복수형이에요. little과 a little은 셀 수 없는 명사 앞에 써요.

items.q: Travis가 한 말의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 길 밖으로 나가서 공룡을 가까이서 봐도 된다.
작은 변화가 미래에 큰 영향을 줄 수 있다.
items.exp: Travis는 You must not leave it at any time.이라고 했으므로 길 밖으로 나가도 된다는 내용은 일치하지 않아요.
items.passage: "Do you see the path over there? You must not leave it at any time. Do not touch anything. You might kill something by accident. A little change here can cause something unthinkable in the future."

choices: I don't have nothing in my bag.
I have anything in my bag.
I don't has anything in my bag.
I doesn't have anything in my bag.
I don't have anything in my bag.
items.exp: 부정문에는 보통 anything을 써요. nothing은 이미 부정의 뜻이라 don't와 함께 쓰지 않고, 긍정문에는 something을 써요. 본문의 Do not touch anything.도 같은 쓰임이에요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 by accident와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
items.exp: by accident는 '실수로, 우연히'라는 뜻이에요. by mistake와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
items.passage: You might kill something [by accident].

items.exp: -thing으로 끝나는 부정대명사는 형용사가 뒤에서 수식해요. (something unthinkable)

choices: Travis는 공룡이 모두 배불러 있다고 말했다.
정글은 안개로 덮여 있었고 매우 조용했다.
Eckels는 겁이 나서 기계에서 내리지 않았다.
일행은 길이 없는 정글로 걸어 들어갔다.
items.exp: The jungle was covered in fog. It was very quiet.에서 확인할 수 있어요. Travis는 일부 공룡이 배고프다고 했어요.
items.passage:
Slowly, everyone got out of the time machine. The jungle was covered in fog. It was very quiet.
"I'm so excited," said Eckels.
"Be careful. Some of the dinosaurs are hungry," said Travis. "Just stay calm. I don't want you to do anything foolish."
"Don't worry. I'm not a fool," said Eckels.
They all began to walk on the path.

items.exp: be covered in[with]는 '~로 덮여 있다'라는 뜻의 수동태 표현이에요.
items.passage: The jungle was covered ( ) fog.

items.q:
빈칸 (A), (B)에 알맞은 말끼리 짝지어진 것은?

The mountain is covered ( A ) snow.
This city is known ( B ) its food.
items.exp: be covered in은 '~로 덮여 있다', be known for는 '~로 유명하다'라는 뜻이에요. be known to는 '~에게 알려져 있다'라서 사람 앞에 써요.
「some of + 복수 명사 + 복수 동사」예요. the dinosaurs가 복수이므로 are를 써요.
items.passage: Be careful. Some of the dinosaurs ( ) hungry.

choices: I want to you be careful.
I want that you are careful.
I want you to be careful.
items.exp: want + 목적어 + to부정사는 '(목적어)가 ~하기를 원하다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 부분과 의미가 같은 문장은?
choices: They all began walking on the path.
They all began walk on the path.
They all began to walking on the path.
They all began walked on the path.
They all begin walking on the path.
items.exp: begin은 to부정사와 동명사를 모두 목적어로 취해요. began to walk = began walking이에요.
items.passage: They all [began to walk] on the path.

choices: T. rex는 Eckels 가까이에서 자고 있었다.
T. rex는 100미터 떨어진 곳에 천천히 나타났다.
items.exp: One hundred meters away, a T. rex slowly appeared.에서 확인할 수 있어요. Eckels는 겁에 질렸고, Travis는 조용히 하라고 했어요.
items.passage:
After some time, Travis whispered, "Look over there. There is a T. rex."
One hundred meters away, a T. rex slowly appeared.
"It," whispered Eckels. "It ..."
"Sh!"
"It ... is huge. I've never seen such a huge thing. I'm so scared," said Eckels.
"Sh ... quiet!" Travis said angrily. "You don't want it to see you."
"I can't breathe," said Eckels. "Get me out of here!"

items.q: 밑줄 친 I've never seen의 용법과 같은 것은?
items.exp: never와 함께 '~한 적이 없다'를 나타내는 현재완료는 경험 용법이에요.
items.passage: [I've never seen] such a huge thing.

choices: She is such a kind girl.
She is a such kind girl.
She is such kind a girl.
She is so a kind girl.
items.exp: such + a/an + 형용사 + 명사의 어순이에요.
Travis가 조용히 하라고 한 이유는 T. rex가 Eckels 일행을 보지 못하게 하려는 것이므로 it은 the T. rex예요.
items.passage: "Sh ... quiet!" Travis said angrily. "You don't want [it] to see you."

items.q: 밑줄 친 can't의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: 무서워서 숨을 쉴 수 없다는 뜻이므로 can't는 불가능을 나타내요.
items.passage: "I [can't] breathe," said Eckels. "Get me out of here!"

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말끼리 짝지어진 것은?

He was ( A ) terrified ( B ) he left the path by accident.
items.exp: so + 형용사 + that + 주어 + 동사는 '너무 ~해서 …하다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Eckels가 길을 벗어난 이유로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: He was so terrified that he left the path by accident.에서 확인할 수 있어요.
items.passage:
"Don't panic, Eckels," said Travis. "Turn around, and walk quietly back to the machine."
Eckels turned around and started to run. He was so terrified that he left the path by accident.
"Eckels!" shouted Travis. "Don't leave the path!"
The T. rex heard Travis and turned its head toward him and the other travelers. There was a moment of silence. Then, it suddenly started to run toward them with a loud roar.

items.q: 밑줄 친 the other travelers가 가리키는 것은?
items.exp: the other + 복수 명사는 범위가 정해진 가운데 일부를 제외한 나머지 모두를 가리켜요. 여기서는 Travis와 Eckels를 제외한 나머지 여행자들이에요.
items.passage: The T. rex heard Travis and turned its head toward him and [the other travelers].

items.exp: 고양이가 두 마리로 정해져 있고 하나가 흰색이므로 나머지 한 마리는 the other cat이에요.
items.passage: I have two cats. One is white. ( ) cat is black.

items.q: 다음 중 명사형이 올바르지 않은 것은?
items.exp: -ent로 끝나는 형용사는 -ence로 바꿔 명사를 만들어요. silent의 명사형은 silence예요.

choices: Travis는 Eckels를 두고 먼저 기계로 갔다.
T. rex는 큰 포효와 함께 일행을 향해 달려오기 시작했다.
items.exp: Then, it suddenly started to run toward them with a loud roar.에서 확인할 수 있어요. 일행은 기계로 돌아가 안에 있는 Eckels를 발견했어요.
items.passage:
"Run, everybody! Run!" shouted Travis.
Travis and the other travelers returned safely to the machine and found Eckels inside.
"You put all of us in danger," said Travis to Eckels in an angry voice. "You left the path."
"I'm sorry, but I didn't kill anything," said Eckels. "There's only a little mud on my shoes."

items.exp: put ~ in danger는 '~을 위험에 빠뜨리다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: You put all of us ( ) danger.

items.q: 밑줄 친 in an angry voice와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
items.exp: in an angry voice는 '화난 목소리로'라는 뜻이며 부사 angrily와 같은 뜻이에요.
items.passage: "You put all of us in danger," said Travis to Eckels [in an angry voice].

items.q:
빈칸 (A), (B)에 알맞은 말끼리 짝지어진 것은?

I don't have ( A ).
She found ( B ).
items.exp: 부정문에는 anything, 긍정문에는 something을 써요. nothing은 부정어라서 don't와 함께 쓰지 않아요.
see는 의도와 상관없이 눈에 들어올 때 쓰고, look at·stare at은 전치사 at이 필요해요. can see a mountain처럼 써요.
items.passage: I can ( ) a mountain from here.

choices: He left without to say goodbye.
items.exp: without + 동명사는 '~하지 않고'라는 뜻이에요. 전치사 뒤에는 동명사를 써요.
They all returned to the present safely.에서 확인할 수 있어요. 진흙은 조금 묻어 있다고 했어요.
items.passage:
Travis stared at Eckels for a long time without saying anything.
"Let's go home," said Travis finally.
The machine stopped. They all returned to the present safely.
"Is everything okay here?" asked Travis.
"Fine. Welcome home!" said Mr. Parker.

items.q: 밑줄 친 a little과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: Add a little salt to the soup.
items.exp: 본문의 a little은 셀 수 없는 명사 앞에서 '조금의'라는 뜻이에요. 첫 번째 문장도 같아요. a little girl의 little은 '어린'이라는 형용사예요.
items.passage: There's only [a little] mud on my shoes.

items.exp: everything은 단수로 취급하므로 단수 동사를 써요. 본문의 Is everything okay here?도 be동사 is를 썼어요.

choices: 표지판의 글자가 바뀌어 있었고, 새 대통령은 Mr. Keith가 아니었다.
items.exp: The sign now said "NAIM ANY YEER ..."과 The new president ... was not Mr. Keith.에서 확인할 수 있어요.
items.passage:
Eckels looked around the room carefully. Everything looked the same, except the big sign on the wall. The sign now said, "NAIM ANY YEER EN THE PAST. WEE TAEK YU THAIR." Eckels was confused.
Then, he saw the TV. The new president was on the news, but it was not Mr. Keith.
"What's going on?" He got more confused. He sat down and looked closely at the mud on his shoes.
"No, it can't be," said Eckels. "It's all because of this little thing?" He was shocked.
In the mud on his right shoe, he found a small dead butterfly.

items.exp: 표지판의 문구 철자가 달라진 것을 보고 Eckels was confused.라고 했어요.
items.passage:
Eckels looked around the room carefully. Everything looked the same, except the big sign on the wall. The sign now said, "NAIM ANY YEER EN THE PAST. WEE TAEK YU THAIR." Eckels was confused.
Then, he saw the TV. The new president was on the news, but it was not Mr. Keith.
"What's going on?" He got more confused. He sat down and looked closely at the mud on his shoes.
"No, it can't be," said Eckels. "It's all because of this little thing?" He was shocked.
In the mud on his right shoe, he found a small dead butterfly.

items.q:
빈칸 (A), (B)에 알맞은 말끼리 짝지어진 것은?

He was shocked ( A ) this little thing.
He was shocked ( B ) he saw the butterfly.
items.exp: because of 뒤에는 명사(구), because 뒤에는 「주어 + 동사」가 와요.
-ed/-ing 형태의 형용사의 비교급은 앞에 more를 붙여요. get + 비교급은 '더 ~해지다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 can't와 의미가 같은 것은?
choices: He can't be a doctor. He is only ten.
We can't use phones in class.
items.exp: 본문의 can't be는 '~일 리가 없다'라는 강한 부정의 추측이에요. 첫 번째 문장도 같은 뜻이에요. 나머지는 불가능이나 금지예요.
items.passage: "No, it [can't] be," said Eckels.

items.q: 밑줄 친 found와 의미가 같은 것은?
choices: I found my lost key under the sofa.
The city was founded by a king.
items.exp: 본문의 found는 find(발견하다)의 과거형이에요. 첫 번째 문장도 같은 뜻이에요. 나머지는 found(설립하다)의 과거형·과거분사 founded예요.
items.passage: In the mud on his right shoe, he [found] a small dead butterfly.

items.q: Eckels가 마지막에 발견한 것으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 오른쪽 신발의 진흙 속 작은 죽은 나비
왼쪽 신발의 진흙 속 살아 있는 나비
items.exp: In the mud on his right shoe, he found a small dead butterfly.에서 확인할 수 있어요.
items.passage:
Eckels looked around the room carefully. Everything looked the same, except the big sign on the wall. The sign now said, "NAIM ANY YEER EN THE PAST. WEE TAEK YU THAIR." Eckels was confused.
Then, he saw the TV. The new president was on the news, but it was not Mr. Keith.
"What's going on?" He got more confused. He sat down and looked closely at the mud on his shoes.
"No, it can't be," said Eckels. "It's all because of this little thing?" He was shocked.
In the mud on his right shoe, he found a small dead butterfly.

choices: He asked what could he do.
He asked what he do could.
He asked what he could do.
He asked he could do what.
He asked what did he do.
items.exp: ask의 목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문은 「의문사 + 주어 + 동사」의 어순이에요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 부분에서 you 앞에 생략된 것은?
items.exp: nothing을 꾸미는 관계대명사절 you can do 앞에 목적격 관계대명사 that이 생략되어 있어요.
items.passage: "Well, there's nothing [you can do]," said Travis.

items.q:
빈칸 (A), (B)에 알맞은 말끼리 짝지어진 것은?

In 2023, a 101-year-old time capsule ( A ) at a high school in Canada. It ( B ) inside the school's walls in 1922.
items.exp: 타임캡슐은 '열린' 것이고 '묻힌' 것이므로 모두 「be동사 + 과거분사」인 수동태를 써요.
items.passage: In 2023, a 101-year-old time capsule was opened at a high school in Canada. It was buried inside the school's walls in 1922. Many old items like newspapers were found in the time capsule.

items.q: 밑줄 친 has come true와 같은 용법의 현재완료가 쓰인 문장은?
choices: I have lived here for ten years.
I have never seen a ghost.
He has been sick since Monday.
We have known each other for years.
She has lost her key, so she can't open the door.
items.exp: has come true는 과거에 일어난 일이 현재까지 영향을 미치는 결과 용법이에요. 첫 번째 문장도 열쇠를 잃어버려서 지금 문을 못 연다는 결과예요.
items.passage:
Dear Future Me,
Hi. How are you? I'm now in the second grade in middle school. You've always wanted to be a pilot. I hope your dream [has come true]. Hope you're happy.
With love,
Mina
